title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
author: Aesop
source: Public domain. Retold from Aesop's Fables.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, there was a shepherd boy who watched over a flock of sheep on a hillside near his village. All day long he sat under a tree, and all day long the sheep nibbled the grass. The boy thought it was very, very boring.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One afternoon, the boy had an idea for a trick. He jumped up, cupped his hands around his mouth, and shouted down to the village,

segments.speaker: boy
segments.text: "Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is chasing the sheep!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The villagers dropped everything and came running up the hill to help. But when they arrived, there was no wolf at all — only the boy, laughing and laughing.

segments.speaker: boy
segments.text: "There is no wolf! I fooled you all!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he giggled. The villagers grumbled and walked back down the hill.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A few days later, the boy grew bored again.

segments.speaker: boy
segments.text: "Wolf! Wolf!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he shouted, even louder than before. Once more the villagers came running, and once more they found the boy laughing at his trick.

segments.speaker: villagers
segments.text: "You should not cry wolf when there is no wolf,"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they warned him, and they went back to their work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, one evening as the sun was setting, a real wolf crept out of the forest. The sheep bleated and scattered in fear. The boy leapt to his feet.

segments.speaker: boy
segments.text: "Wolf! Wolf! Please, help! A real wolf!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he cried with all his might.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But down in the village, the people only shook their heads.

segments.speaker: villagers
segments.text: "He is trying to fool us again,"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they said, and nobody came. The wolf scattered the whole flock before loping back into the woods.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The next morning, the boy sadly told the villagers what had truly happened. A kind old farmer put a hand on his shoulder and said,

segments.speaker: farmer
segments.text: "Nobody believes someone who tells lies — even when they are telling the truth."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And from that day on, the boy only ever called for help when he really needed it.
